title: Renewal Risk Assessment & Exec Escalation Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft of the Renewal Risk Assessment & Executive Escalation Playbook used by the Customer Success organization. Goal: create a repeatable, time-bound process for identifying at-risk renewals, diagnosing root causes, and driving prioritized remediation (technical, commercial, executive) to preserve ARR.

Scope:
- Applies to all ARR renewals > $25k ARR and strategic accounts flagged by Sales/Admin.
- Focused on the 90-day window prior to contract renewal.
- Intended for CSMs, AMs, Solutions Engineers, and GTM leadership.

How to use this doc:
- Use as the canonical checklist for renewal-focused QBR prep and weekly risk syncs.
- Update the customer-specific tracker row and attach a short summary to the QBR doc.
- Escalate per the ladder below when decision criteria are met.

1) Renewal Risk Signals (monitor these continuously)
- Usage decline: rolling 30d active seat / token volume down > 30% vs prior 90d
- Increased latency or error reports correlated with customer incidents (>= 3 incidents/month)
- Cost surprise or unexpected bills complaints from customer finance
- Product misfit for new use-cases (feature gap, model quality regression)
- Renewing team change or sponsor turnover
- Security/compliance blockers (audit, SOC2 evidence delays)
- Competitive displacement signals (RFPs, cool-down of feature requests)

2) Risk Scoring Rubric (simple, shared score)
- Severity (0–3): 0=none, 1=low, 2=medium, 3=high
- Impacted ARR (0–3): 0=<10k, 1=10–50k, 2=50–250k, 3=>250k
- Time-sensitivity (0–2): 0=>60 days, 1=30–60 days, 2=<30 days
- Exec attention modifier (+1): sponsor change or security issue
- Total score = sum (0–9).
  - Low risk: 0–2 (monitor)
  - Medium risk: 3–5 (action plan, weekly sync)
  - High risk: 6+ (immediate escalation)

3) Immediate Triage Steps (first 72 hours when flagged)
- Owner: CSM (within 24h)
  - Quick intake note in tracker: describe signal, last contact date, renewal date, ARR, sponsor(s).
  - Send short check-in email to primary sponsor asking to confirm health and any blockers.
  - Pull product telemetry: DAU, tokens/day, error rate, model quality regressions, latency P95 for last 14 days.
  - Review open support tickets and their SLA status.
  - Score risk using rubric and update tracker.

4) Escalation Ladder (who to pull in and when)
- CSM: routine triage, owner of customer relationship and QBRs.
- Account Executive / AM: engaged when contract terms, renewal upsell, or pricing plays required (score >= 3).
- Solutions Engineer (SE): engage for technical root cause, performance tuning, quantization/throughput workarounds (score >= 3 or technical incident).
- Customer Exec Sponsor (internal): request intros/engagement with customer execs when sponsor change or exec-level risk (modifier +1) and score >= 5.
- VP Customer Success / CRO: pull when score >= 6 or high-profile strategic accounts (board-level risk).
- Legal & Security: loop in immediately if compliance or data residency are blockers.

Escalation etiquette: 
- Always include CSM summary + risk score + 1-paragraph ask in escalation threads.
- Provide proposed mitigation options and required customer commitments.
- Set a clear next-action owner and 48-hour due date.

5) Common Scenarios & Recommended Save Plays
A. Budget / Cost Pressure
  - Actions: run cost-of-inference analysis, propose cost controls (burst caps, routing to cheaper model variant), offer 3–6 month stepped pricing discount tied to usage recovery, or pilot workload optimization with Redwood Optimize (no-fee pilot).
  - Template ask: short commercial proposal + ROI projection attached.
  - Who: CSM + AE + Finance ops.

B. Usage Drop (adoption issues)
  - Actions: run a 30-day re-onboarding campaign, host "Make it Work" workshop with SEs, create adoption OKRs, deliver playbook for power users, schedule weekly enablement calls.
  - Offer: complimentary enablement hours (up to N), success milestones tied to renewal.
  - Who: CSM + SE + Customer Success Enablement.

C. Performance / Reliability Problems
  - Actions: priority incident remediation, create joint RCA, commit fixed timeline for fix or mitigation (fallback routing, model swap), provide credits for downtime if appropriate.
  - Who: SRE / Serving Runtime + SE + CSM.

D. Security & Compliance Blocker
  - Actions: engage security/compliance immediately, surface evidence pack (SOC2 artifacts, KMS options), propose Private deployment path if necessary (timeline, cost).
  - Who: Security, Legal, VP CS.

E. Competitive Displacement
  - Actions: get on-call competitive intel from AE, offer short-term product roadmap commitments (time-bound), offer sandboxes for new use-cases, exec-to-exec meeting within 7 days.
  - Who: AE + CSM + Product sponsor.

6) Play Examples (concrete text to use)
- Exec outreach subject: "Brief: {{Customer}} renewal — request 30 min to align on path forward"
- Exec outreach body (short):
  Hi {{ExecName}},

  Quick note — as {{Customer}} approaches renewal on {{renewal_date}} we want to ensure there are no outstanding blockers. We’ve identified a few adoption and cost items that we’d like to align on and propose a short remediation plan. Can you join a 30-minute discussion with our VP CS and technical lead next week?

  Proposed agenda: 1) Current usage & cost picture 2) Customer priorities for next 12 months 3) Proposed short-term remediation & success milestones

  Thanks,
  {{CSM}}

- Save play: "Usage Recovery Sprint" (2–4 weeks)
  - Deliverables: customized onboarding + dashboard, weekly progress reviews, SE-led tuning session, 1x exec checkpoint at 2 weeks, success criteria = 20% usage recovery or signed plan to embed within roadmap.

7) Renewal Tracker (recommended columns for the team sheet)
- Customer Name, Account Owner (CSM), AE, ARR, Renewal Date, Renewal Window (90/60/30), Risk Score, Risk Category, Last Contact, Last QBR Date, Open Issues (short), Proposed Save Play, Current Offer, Next Action Owner, Next Action Due, Notes/History (one line).

8) QBR Prep Checklist (for renewal-focused QBRs)
- One-page health summary + risk score (to include in QBR deck)
- Telemetry snapshot (usage, errors, latency)
- Business outcomes map (how customer measures success)
- Open issues + commitments tracker + timeline
- Commercial summary: pricing, credits, proposed terms
- Recommended next steps + requested customer commitments

9) Decision criteria for immediate exec escalation
- Risk score >= 6 OR
- Security/compliance blocker OR
- Incidence of executive sponsor change AND ARR > 100k OR
- Competitive RFP in active consideration AND time to renewal < 30 days

10) Timing / Suggested Cadence (90-day play timeline)
- Day -90: initial risk flagging, CSM triage, basic data capture in tracker.
- Day -60: in-depth QBR prep, technical review if required, engage AE.
- Day -45: deliver commercial options, usage recovery play start if adoption issue.
- Day -30: exec outreach if score >= 5, legal review for changes, finalize offer if discounting.
- Day -14: final negotiated terms, exec check-in.
- Day -7: closure or formal churn plan (if unresolved escalate to VP CS / CRO).

11) Metrics to surface in weekly renewals syncs
- Risk distribution (count by low/medium/high)
- Number of at-risk accounts with >30d open blockers
- Average time from flag to first customer contact
- % of saves that required exec involvement

12) Handoffs & Ownership
- CSM: primary owner for all customer contact, tracker updates, QBR prep.
- AE: commercial proposals, discount approvals, renewal contract negotiation.
- SE / SRE: technical mitigation, incident ownership.
- VP CS / CRO: final decision authority on escalated commercial concessions.

13) Quick Templates (copyable)
- CSM check-in (short):
  Subject: Quick check — {{Customer}} renewal
  Body: Hi {{Sponsor}},

  Quick one-line check: are you seeing any blockers to the upcoming renewal on {{renewal_date}}? We’ve prepared a short set of options to address cost and adoption items; happy to walk through next week.

- Offer summary snippet (for AE use):
  - 6-month stepped discount: Month 1–2: 35% off, Month 3–6: 20% off; rev share for backlog projects; winback criteria: usage recovers to baseline by month 3.

14) Open questions / TODOs (work items for this doc)
- Standardize discount approval thresholds with Finance (who can sign what at what ARR band).
- Create a short tracker template (sheet) and automate risk score calc from telemetry.
- Draft a "Customer Evidence Pack" template for security asks (SOC2 snippets, KMS options, private deployment checklist).
- Workshop retention plays with Sales and Product to agree on "exec ask" commitments we can make.

Notes (working):
- Keep the playbook lightweight — primary value is speed; escalate early with clear asks rather than long analysis.
- We should store final offers and any exceptions in the contract notes tab in Salesforce.

Attachments to include with customer row in tracker:
- Latest QBR deck link, telemetry snapshot CSV, open incident list, proposed commercial term sheet.

If you use this doc: please add notes inline and mark sections you think should be formalized into the team handbook.

Saved drafts / related: see linked artifacts above.

-- Aisha (CSM lead) 2026-03-10
